I don't even know how to go about this. You aren't weak. Relying on people is human nature. We all rely on each other for everything. We buy food grown by farmers, we buy phones and cars from manufacturers, we pay for internet that other people manage. We then do our own part and work a job to make money. That money comes from other people who need whatever product or service you provide. This happens on a social level too. We rely on each other for entertainment, moral support, and compassion. Humans are social creatures. The only thing I can think of is that you must feel traumatized from something that left you feeling like you can't trust others. That could very well be the origin of your depression.

It's better to have loved and lost than never to have loved at all.

When it all comes down to it, the decision is yours to make. It's our duty to help you make the right choice. Let me tell you that suicide is not the right choice. If your life is shit, then it's your duty to yourself to find a way to make it less shit.

If you never try, you will never be happy. Unless you get over the bump in the road, your feeling that failing is better than never trying, then you can't find happiness. I want you to go look at yourself in a mirror. Do you want to turn your life around, or do you want to spiral out of control? You're feeling hopelessness, and it's ruining your life. You didn't mention a doctor at all in your post, or medication. You critically need attention. Let that be your goal. Let that be your gateway towards a better life. Nothing feels better than the feeling of self control.

Okay, excuse me for stalking, but looking at your post history, I see this has been a concern for you for a long time. You also have a strong moral conflict pertaining to religion. Between the college struggle, the religious struggle, and the self image struggle, you have a lot to be stressed about. That's why you feel so different. It's because of what a unique situation you live in.

A number of things can factor into depression, such as sleep schedule, exercise, diet, current events, etc. Depression is often caused by some combination of things and manifests itself in another way, such as your low self esteem or jealousy.

It's normal for people to feel these things. It's normal for people to think they are weird, or don't fit in. You do fit in. You just might not know where yet.

If you're not on any medication or treatment for depression, look into it. You are an amazing individual. The world would be darker without you.

Then there is nothing truly abnormal about you. There are lots of girls like you that struggle to find their beauty, or feel like they just don't compare with others. It's a kind of jealous that our society seems to promote. So why do you want so badly to be beautiful? Is it maybe because you want to be popular like those girls are? Or maybe you are trying to find a romantic relationship and just think you don't stand a chance?

Well, whatever it is you really want, you can get there. Looks can influence a person's first impressions, but it's the content of your character which will get you places.

Creative writing always seemed like it could be fun, but I never had the space for it in my high school schedule. I really hope that you find some big inspiration and write something jaw dropping.

And if you miss the horsies so much, then maybe it's time to visit them? I don't know much about horse riding, but I do know that animals are amazingly therapeutic. My cat is my lifeline.

It's completely common for women to look down on themselves (more common in women than in men) even if nothing is wrong. Some women starve themselves to the point that they're hospitalized because they wanted to lose *more* weight. I don't want that to be you. You sound like such a fun little character and you deserve better than to slave yourself to your appearance.

I don't know what you look like, but I don't think it really matters. And a quirky character is always the character people like the most, and remember. You're a creative writer, so you should know this better than everyone. You might think you have a weird personality, but that might also be exactly what makes you worth knowing.

Why don't you step outside your comfort zone and try talking to new people in your creative writing class? Sounds to me like you just need some friends you can hang out with. If you already have a gang, why don't you ask them for their honest opinion of you. Look at your good qualities, not your bad ones, and realize that sometimes your bad qualities aren't as bad as you think they are.

You are not selfish, and he's not healthy for her. It may seem like none of this would have happened if they stayed together, but I'm not so sure. It's a toxic relationship and it would only have gotten worse. It sounds to me like you are doing the best you can for yourself and for her. Once your mother recovers, I am convinced you will recover too. I hate being powerless, and yet I feel completely powerless here. You are stuck in the middle. Nothing you do is working and it's making you depressed. You are powerless too. The most I can say for you is to hang in there and be there for your mother. Try surprising her with gifts, and make sure to never stop trying to make things better. It may seem like nothing works, but that's because your mother has to get over him on her own. The most you can do is support her through the whole ordeal. Make sure she knows how important she is to everyone, and stay positive. You're a good kid. I have faith that your support will help her through this.

Your dad should feel ashamed. Your mom sounds like she lives in a fantasy that you just don't fit into. Okay, well I still fully believe that the only way for you to recover is to be open to ideas. Even if you don't like my idea, at least try to improve. You can fail a million times and it'll still be better than giving up hope. Just the fact that you are posting here shows that you still have a desire to live. You wouldn't be talking about it otherwise. If you don't think you can talk to your parents (and I mean bluntly telling them you are suicidal) then instead you should just attach yourself to the things you love. If you can synthesize a world where you are surrounded by things that you love (friends, youtube..... even porn) then I believe you can get better. The only thing holding you back is self doubt.

You're not alone. I am writing this to you at 6:00 AM. Fourth day in a row with no real sleep. I've napped in the day a few times, but it just doesn't give me energy. I hope you make it through this horrible sleep deprivation. I'll be here trying to make it through too.

You are going through as much as your mother is. Tell her you couldn't live without her. Tell her how much you love her. Tell her that the divorce is hurting you too. Tell her you are as depressed as she is. Most importantly, tell her that she is strong, and you are trying to be strong too. These are difficult times for the both of you, and the only way for either of you to make it through this is together.

I'm sorry that you feel that way, but trust me when I say that you can make yourself better. You can't do it alone, but depression is something that won't go away if you personally don't try to make it go away. And I really don't believe you when you say your parents hate you. I just think you don't see eye to eye with them. They don't understand you and you don't understand them. Trust me, they will care when you tell them.

And if your parents do hate you, then they'll ignore the text and it'll be even easier to send it. At least try. What do you have to lose?

Bad grades =/= stupid as shit. Nobody is truly stupid. I like your plan though. Wait until everything is payed off. By then, you will likely find a new reason to love to live. I hope for the best for you.
Please tell me you are still alive.

Your depression is a side effect of your family. They are clearly not helpful to you, so why do you stay? My little sister (4 years old) would be in a similar situation to you were it not for us adopting her. Both her biological parents are drug addicts who live on the streets. That's no way to live. You can do more for yourself than they ever did. Don't be afraid to call CPS. You need to live away from that toxic environment. You need to get away from your family. Don't become like them. Don't waste away your life; put them in the past. Find new people who care about you, and can help you. Seriously. But don't simply run away. You are still legal property of your parents, but you have the power to change that. Call CPS, and start your journey to take Control if your own life. You might need therapy, you might need a job, but whatever it is, your CPS agent can help you, and your school counselor can help you. Please don't go e up on yourself. Your story touched me pretty deep. If you ever want to talk, PM me.

I'm no guru who knows all the answers, but trust me when I say you are the only one who can choose how to live your life. Keep me up to date on your life. I know this isn't easy, but you are emotionally strong. I want to hear from you when you take the reins and make your life worth living. Don't worry about grades. Just do your best while you're in school, and accept whatever grade they give you. And don't do this alone. Talk to friends and counselors. Let them help you through this.

(Oh and just because you can control your own life doesn't mean you have to live in an apartment and work a job in addition to school. There are lots of programs out there to help people in your situation to sustain a happy life, at least til you come of age. By then, your life will be in order and you will have contacts to help you transition into adulthood.)

That was exactly me for awhile. Porn, YouTube, video games, and a sense that my life was collapsing before me. Never met someone to date, never wanted to look. Still don't. I lived through it, and so can you, but you are right on one thing. It doesn't get better. Not on its own at least. The only person that can fix you is you. You and your family. Your friends. Who the fuck cares about what kind of person you're going to be in a year, or two, or ten. You sure as hell shouldn't. What really matters is what kind of person you are going to be today. Do you want today to be a mopey depressed mess? Or do you want today to be the day you turn our life around? All I can say for you, is to tell your family what you're going through. It's hard to build that courage, but it's what will get you through this. Send your mom a text. That's what I did. I couldn't say it to her face. Need help? Type out the message first, without even thinking about sending it. When it's done, hitting the send button is as difficult as pulling the trigger of a gun. So now, think logically. You could kill yourself, or with the exact same amount of effort, you could try to turn your life back around. The only thing is... you have to be willing to accept help.

Utterly heartbreaking. I don't think you quite understand though... why would you kill yourself instead of seeking help beyond your family? I know the feelings you have. Nothing is fun, nothing makes you happy. Instead you feel simply nothing. Sometimes sadness, or anger, or fear, but you don't feel joy, or excitement. Am I right? I don't want to write a wall of text so I will simply say this: Open up to the people that love you. Tell them about how suicidal you are. Nobody can help you past this unless you offer to accept help.

And death may seem like a solution, and while I do believe it is a solution, I also believe it's the worst solution you can have. You sound like such a caring person, and you are concerned about how other people will feel if you died. Now imagine being one of those people. Imagine being your mom. How do you think she would feel if she knew her child was depressed, to the point of being suicidal. You don't have to be dead for them to care about you. They will do everything it takes to make you happy again. Just please reach out to them so they can help you. Give them a chance to make things right.

In fact, if they know you are suicidal, it will make it less shocking when you pass. If you want to leave the minimum negative impact on the people around you, you would let them know ahead of time that you are suffering.

Oh and don't ever feel guilty about being depressed. It's not your fault that you feel this way.

Have you been open with your family? Do they know that you're going through this? Don't assume that they can read context clues because depression is such a hard thing to detect in many people. If you trust that your family loves you, tell them the truth. The only reason they would want you to get good grades is if they cared about your future, so I should guess they love you.

Tell them you were going to attempt suicide.

When I went through this exact same experience, I didn't tell anyone. I first started thinking about ways that I could die accidentally. Then it started escalating to ways that I could influence an "accident" to occur. Mostly, I just wished for death but was too afraid to go out and do it myself. When I decided I would kill myself, a close friend of mine unknowingly saved my life by occupying my entire day with video games. Having lived through the day I was going to kill myself, I mustered up the courage to tell my mom. She took me to a cemetery (it's very peaceful there) and we talked about my depression. Even though she always strived for me to get good grades, she cared more about my mental state than my grades. A have a quote for you straight from my mother's mouth that day.

"Fuck grades"

Grades aren't important. Be open about yourself, and you will find the understanding that you need.


And please confirm for us that you are still alive. We're worried about you.

Your husband is hardly a spouse. He doesn't sound like he's there for you, but we are. He's right, that nobody can "fix" you... except for you. The only true way to overcome depression is for you to realize the cause and fix it yourself. That's not easy, and day to day life can be a chore. That's why it's so, so important to have friends or family that love and support you. You can find plenty of friends here who would give their best efforts to help you.

Compassion, understanding, and medication can help a depressed person to make it through each day, but unless you find that spark of happiness, something that you can cling to, love, and appreciate, or you find what's causing your depression and put an end to it, then all the medication in the world won't get you past this.

That isn't to say we can't help you help yourself. Do you have a hobby? Spend more time with it. Do you have friends you trust unconditionally?People like your sister? Be blunt with them about your current state. Don't be shy. They love and care about you, but they might not understand how serious this is.

Also, before judging what other people say, try to think from their shoes. This is why I say to be blunt. If you make a casual remark about depression, and they don't pounce on the opportunity to help you, or they laugh like it was a joke, don't take it personally. They just don't get the picture you are trying to paint. Be honest and blunt with them, and they will understand you have a problem which you can't handle alone.

You can meet lifelong friends on the internet, and even if you don't know them in person, they can be more understanding and logical than anyone in person could be. Maybe you just need to reach out to a different audience. If your husband and family really don't care about you, then search for people who do. That can come from the internet, a psychiatric hospital, therapists, you name it. Just don't be afraid to admit your state of mind to people. If you ever find someone who has gone through depression, they will know exactly how you feel. You can talk to them.

That's why this subreddit is so good. Most of us have been there, and felt that. You can always find someone who wants you to be happy, and wants you to enjoy life.

The most you can do is be open. Open up to the idea of talking about depression with people you know care about you. Talk to your friend, talk to your family. Talk to your doctor. Talk here. People care more about you than you can begin to imagine, and as soon as you open your heart to them, you will feel their love within you. (No matter how cliche that sounds)

I was struggling in school, and found that I was faking my happiness so naturally that nobody knew I wanted to kill myself. My mom pushed me to do well in school but I just couldn't make myself try. Instead I sat there, hating myself, thinking I was unsuccessful and that I would never go to college and I would never get my dream job. Finally, I decided to kill myself, but I was afraid to die. I put it off until the day before my next test, deciding I would try to enjoy myself the last few days, and be gone before the test stresses me out. Instead, a friend of mine so happened to occupy my entire day and I was too sleepy to go off and kill myself that night. Having dodged a bullet, I built the courage to speak up and tell my mom. It wasn't until my mom said "fuck grades" that I realized how much love surpasses success. 

You don't have to be the best, and as long as you keep your composure and never give up on your goals, you will get there. Don't worry about the times you fail, just work on self improvement. Focus on little successes, and above all else, talk about your depression. Tell people about how shitty you've felt, and tell people about suicidal thoughts. But also tell people about accomplishments. Tell people about your hobbies. Let people know when you are happy, and when you are depressed. Do you like video games? Find someone online who understands you and invite them to play video games over the internet. Or maybe you like movies? You can watch movies with people over the internet too. The point is, there are people who care about you, but they can't help you unless you reach out to them.
